Title: Scaffold monorepo structure
Description: Create the repository layout described in ARD v2.0.0 Appendix A: api/ for Vercel serverless entrypoints, finhive/ for the Python package, web/ for the React SPA, dbt/, migrations/, evals/, tests/. Add pyproject.toml, package.json, and .gitignore. Acceptance: both python -m pytest and npm run build succeed on an empty scaffold.

Title: Build the orchestrator build loop
Description: Implement ops/orchestrator.sh: walk queue.tsv in dependency order, branch feature/fin-N from the top of the stack, run the implementing agent, invoke the CodeRabbit CLI gate pre-push, return blocking findings to the agent for at most CR_MAX_ROUNDS (2) rounds, then mediate — fix, dismiss with rationale, or escalate to a new Linear issue carrying every attempted fix and why it failed. Open a stacked PR. Nothing merges without a human. Carry the AssetAuditor hard-won rules: take ops/.worktree.lock around every checkout, re-exec from TMPDIR because the script rewrites its own worktree, and pick the stack tip by commits-ahead-of-development rather than commit date. Acceptance: a single queued issue runs end to end and opens a PR with the gate evidence attached.

Title: Build run_builder.sh guard wrapper
Description: Implement ops/run_builder.sh as the entry point that decides whether a build pass is warranted: exit quietly if another builder is running, if an issue is in flight (worktree lock held), or if the queue is exhausted; otherwise continue the stack from the deepest unmerged feature branch. Support --status for a read-only view of queue, locks and recent log. Reclaim a builder lock only when it is old enough that the process behind it cannot plausibly be alive. Acceptance: concurrent invocations do not both start, and --status touches no lock.

Title: Build the CodeRabbit PR gate publisher
Description: Implement ops/pr_gate.sh. The CLI gate runs pre-push, so a PR's fix commits are already in its first commit set and the findings sit in gitignored logs — from GitHub the result is an unverifiable claim with no check behind it. Republish per PR every finding by round, the commit that answered it, and the final re-review, then set a coderabbit/cli-gate commit status. Status is success only when the final round returned zero blocking findings. Make it a required check on development. It must need no Claude — bash, gh and the logs only — so it still works when spend is capped. Acceptance: an unreviewed or unresolved branch cannot merge.

Title: Gitignore ops lock directories and local state
Description: git clean -fd removes untracked DIRECTORIES, and the orchestrator runs it two lines after taking ops/.worktree.lock — an unignored lock deletes itself and mutual exclusion silently stops working. Add ops/.builder.lock/, ops/.worktree.lock/, ops/logs/, ops/.env.local, ops/queue.tsv, ops/.completed_issues and ops/.review_debt.tsv to .gitignore before the first orchestrator run. Acceptance: git status is clean while a lock is held.

Title: Write the developer agent operating contract
Description: Document the agentic development loop from ARD section 18: branch from development as feature/xx-N, implement, invoke CodeRabbit CLI, fix blocking findings for a maximum of two cycles, then escalate by filing a Linear issue containing the finding, each attempted fix, why it failed, and a suggested direction. Acceptance: the contract is merged and referenced from CLAUDE.md.

Title: Land MVP1 source on main and reconcile model names
Description: The Claude Design sync read the repository at main and found only .gitignore and LICENSE. MVP1 source lives on development. Consequently every Pydantic model name in ARD v2.1.0 section 2 is a proposal, not a reconciled name, and the v2.0.0 claim that main is always deployable is true only degenerately. Merge MVP1 to main, then reconcile all 38 binding model names against the real finhive package. Acceptance: main contains the source and the ARD binding table cites real model names.

Title: Configure GitHub Actions base workflow
Description: Set up .github/workflows/ci.yml with the fast gate tier: ruff, mypy --strict on domain/ and calc/, prettier, eslint, and gitleaks secret scanning. Gates must run in under two minutes and block merge on failure. Order gates cheapest-first so a lint error never burns Groq credits. Acceptance: a PR with a deliberate lint error is blocked in under 30 seconds.

Title: Integrate CodeRabbit CLI into PR workflow
Description: Wire CodeRabbit into the PR pipeline. Configure .coderabbit.yaml with path filters, review instructions referencing the FinHive coding conventions, and a clear blocking vs advisory severity split. The CLI must be invokable locally as coderabbit review --plain so the developer agent can consume findings programmatically. Acceptance: opening a PR triggers a CodeRabbit review and blocking findings prevent merge.

Title: Add SQL injection CI grep gate
Description: Add a CI step that scans for f-strings, percent formatting, and .format() inside SQL string constants and fails the build on any match. This is the primary compensating control for choosing raw SQL over an ORM. Acceptance: a PR introducing an f-string in a SQL constant is blocked.

Title: Implement import-linter architecture boundary contracts
Description: Add import-linter contracts to pyproject.toml enforcing the service boundaries from ARD section 5: calc-service must be pure (no asyncpg, httpx, or agent imports), agent-service must never import asyncpg or finhive.db.raw directly, and domain must not import infrastructure or presentation. Acceptance: CI fails when a boundary-violating import is introduced.

Title: Configure stacked PR workflow
Description: Establish development as the integration base and main as always-deployable. Feature branches stack on development; a release PR promotes development to main. Configure branch protection requiring all gates plus one human approval. Acceptance: direct pushes to main are blocked and the release flow is documented.

Title: MVP1 multi-select ByMonth filter in the Interest Calculator
Description: Business requirement: the Interest Calculator currently allows selecting only ONE month from the ByMonth filter, implemented as single-selection radio buttons. Users need to report across several months at once. Replace the radio group with multi-selection checkboxes and change the filter predicate from equality on a single month to membership in a selected set. Success metric: with several months selected, every loan whose due_date month falls in ANY selected month appears in the filtered set, and no others. Preserve every existing rule — ByMonth still excludes records with no due_date, still scopes to the current calendar year, and still includes Overdue records. Select-none must behave exactly as today's no-filter case, not as select-all. This changes MVP1, which is the live system, so it ships behind the MVP1 regression gate with new unit tests for the set-membership predicate. Do this BEFORE the MVP2 calculator is built so MVP2 replicates the new behaviour rather than building single-select and reworking it. Acceptance: selecting Mar and Jul returns exactly the union of both months' records; existing single-month behaviour is preserved when one box is ticked; MVP1 suite green.

Title: MVP1 regression gate on every pull request
Description: Business continuity is the number one constraint: the MVP1 user validates real business on the development branch throughout MVP2 development, and MVP1 functionality must not regress. Add a required CI job running the full MVP1 suite (150 unit and integration tests plus 22 smoke tests) against src/Loan Manager on every PR, regardless of which paths changed. A PR that breaks the desktop app cannot merge. This is the mechanism that makes business continuity a property of the pipeline rather than a hope. Acceptance: a deliberate break in MVP1 domain code blocks an unrelated MVP2 PR.

Title: Freeze the five open contract decisions
Description: ARD v2.1.0 section 10 raises five contract decisions with recommendations: viewer agent access (yes, read-only tools), optimistic concurrency (yes, If-Match plus 409), report async threshold (100), revert as a first-class endpoint (yes, and not an agent tool), and pagination (cursor across all six list endpoints). These block contract freeze and several implementation tickets. Acceptance: each decision is recorded in the ARD decision log and the dependent tickets are unblocked.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Local development setup for macOS and Windows
Description: The milestone-one deliverable: a developer or the MVP1 user can run the whole web app locally on either OS. Provide run_local_mac.sh and run_local_windows.bat that check runtime versions, create the Python virtualenv, install backend and frontend dependencies, start Postgres locally (or connect to a Supabase branch), apply migrations, seed the service account, and launch the API and SPA together. Write the matching setup guide for each OS under docs/. Mirror the MVP1 launcher conventions, including the version check with a readable failure message. Acceptance: a clean machine reaches a working local app from a single command on both operating systems.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Build forward-only SQL migration runner
Description: Implement the numbered migration system: migrations/NNNN_name.sql applied in order, with a schema_migrations table recording version, checksum, and applied_at. CI must fail if a previously-applied file's checksum changes. No down migrations. Acceptance: running the migrator twice is idempotent and editing an applied migration fails CI.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Create orgs and users tables with multi-tenancy
Description: Migration 0001: create orgs and users tables. users maps Supabase auth.users to an org_id and a role of owner, bookkeeper, or viewer. Acceptance: a user can be created and resolved to an org and role.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Port MVP1 schema to Postgres with org_id
Description: Migration 0002: port the six MVP1 tables (loans, loan_meta, loan_history, reports, report_records, report_meta) to Postgres, adding org_id to every business table. Preserve all constraints, indexes, and the reference_id uniqueness guarantee. Acceptance: schema matches the MVP1 data model plus tenancy, and all indexes exist.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Service account login for the MVP1 owner
Description: Milestone one does not need public multi-user auth. Seed a single service account for the existing MVP1 user with role=owner, authenticating against local Supabase Auth, and skip the public signup flow entirely for now. The account must resolve to a real org_id so RLS is exercised from day one rather than bolted on at M4 — a single-tenant shortcut that bypasses RLS would invalidate every isolation guarantee later. Credentials come from ops/.env.local, never committed. Acceptance: the MVP1 user logs in, GET /api/me returns role owner with a real org_id, and RLS filters their queries.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Implement AES-256-GCM encryption at rest for NPI
Description: ADR-2.3 and ADR-2.4 (ARD v2.2.0, v2.3.0). Encrypt every NPI field before it reaches the database, decrypting in the application layer on read: identity fields (borrower_name, depositor_name, borrower_group, depositor_group) AND financial values (amount, interest_amount, commission_amount, tds_amount, chq_amount. Rates and periods stay PLAINTEXT (decisions 13 and 14): a percentage is not a balance, and ADR-2.4 carries the derivation check proving the plaintext columns give no solve path back to amount). Store AES-256-GCM ciphertext with a random 96-bit IV and the auth tag in a _ct column, plus key_version per row. Rejected alternatives are documented in ADR-2.3: pgcrypto puts the key in query logs and lets the database see plaintext; full-disk encryption protects only a powered-off machine; GCM with a random IV alone breaks equality and sorting; deterministic encryption alone still breaks sorting and leaks frequency. Encryption must land BEFORE any real data is written, so no row is ever stored in plaintext and no backfill is needed. Acceptance: no plaintext name or amount appears in the database file, the UI shows real values, and a tampered ciphertext fails the auth tag rather than decrypting to garbage.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Add HMAC blind index for encrypted IDENTITY columns only
Description: ADR-2.3. Exact-match filtering, autocomplete and group auto-fill must keep working on encrypted IDENTITY columns, so store a _bidx column alongside those ciphertexts holding HMAC-SHA256(key_index, normalize(plaintext)) truncated to 16 bytes, where normalize is MVP1's trim-and-lowercase rule so the index is computed over exactly the value MVP1 filters on. Index it. key_index is derived separately from key_data via HKDF with a distinct info string — never reuse one key for both. CRITICAL (ADR-2.4): a blind index must NEVER be added to an amount. Loan amounts cluster on round numbers, so a deterministic index over them is reversible by frequency analysis without the key, and order-preserving encryption is worse because it leaks the full ranking of the loan book. Encode this as a lint rule, not just a comment. Acceptance: MVP1 parity checks A1.1 autocomplete, A1.2 group auto-fill and A5.8 exact filtering pass on identity columns, and a CI rule blocks any derived index on an amount column.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Build key management, derivation and rotation
Description: ADR-2.3. Derive key_data and key_index from a single 32-byte master via HKDF with distinct info strings. For M1a the master lives in ops/.env.local (never committed) or the OS keychain; M3 moves it to Supabase Vault or a KMS fetched at boot and held in memory only. key_version on every row makes rotation incremental: bump the version, encrypt new writes with the new key, migrate old rows in the background, retire the old key when no row references it. A lost key means unrecoverable data, so key backup is part of this ticket rather than an afterthought. Acceptance: a rotation exercise re-encrypts a subset while the app keeps reading both versions, and the documented backup restores a working key.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Encrypt audit JSONB snapshots containing NPI
Description: ADR-2.4. proposed_mutations.before_state and after_state, and agent_turns.react_trace, are JSONB blobs that contain amounts — so they are NPI and must be encrypted at rest like any other financial value. These are also the tables under 7-year retention, so they carry NPI the longest. Encrypt the whole blob with AES-256-GCM rather than per-field, since the shape varies. The approvals diff renderer decrypts in the app layer. Acceptance: no plaintext amount appears in either table's storage and the diff UI still renders field-by-field before and after values.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Add a CI rule banning derived indexes on amount columns
Description: ADR-2.4 names this as the single most likely implementation mistake: copying the identity-column pattern (ciphertext plus blind index) onto an amount. Loan amounts cluster on round numbers, so a deterministic index over them is reversible by frequency analysis without the key, and order-preserving or format-preserving encryption leaks the ranking of the loan book by design. Add a CI check that fails on any _bidx, OPE or FPE column derived from a financial field, and record the rule in the coding standards rather than only in the ADR. Acceptance: a PR adding amount_bidx is blocked with a message explaining why.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Lift MVP1 domain layer unchanged
Description: Move domain/entities, domain/value_objects, domain/services (StatusEngine, InterestCalculator, ReferenceIdService), and domain/repositories interfaces into the MVP2 package file-for-file. No logic changes. Move the corresponding unit tests with them. Acceptance: all MVP1 domain tests pass unchanged with 100 percent coverage on domain services.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Implement asyncpg connection pool with JWT forwarding
Description: Build finhive/db/raw.py: an asyncpg pool that sets request.jwt.claims per connection from the verified JWT so RLS policies evaluate correctly. Handle pool sizing for serverless (small pools, short lifetimes). Acceptance: a query issued through the pool respects RLS for the calling user.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Scaffold FastAPI application with route bundles
Description: Create the FastAPI app split into the four Vercel function bundles from ARD section 7: api/loans, api/reports, api/agent, api/admin. Configure per-bundle timeouts. Wire dependency injection via FastAPI Depends, replacing the MVP1 Container. Acceptance: all four bundles deploy to a Vercel preview and respond to health checks.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Implement JWT verification middleware
Description: Verify Supabase JWTs on every request using cached JWKS. Extract sub and org_id claims into a request-scoped context. Return 401 on invalid or expired tokens. Acceptance: requests without a valid JWT are rejected and valid requests carry org context through to the data layer.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Implement GET api/me role and org bootstrap
Description: Add the endpoint that resolves user_id, org_id, org_name, role and a features array from the verified JWT. This is what makes the RLS model real: role is resolved server-side once rather than inferred per request in the client. Include the features array now as a forward hook for dark-launching capabilities; adding it later is a breaking change. Acceptance: the client caches MeResponse in AuthProvider and every later screen reads role from it.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Decrypt-and-sort path for encrypted columns including amounts
Description: ADR-2.3 and ADR-2.4. Alphabetical sorting on names and NUMERICAL sorting on amount are both MVP1 parity check A2.1, and ciphertext order is neither alphabetical nor numeric. Implement fetch-filtered-set to decrypt to sort to slice in the application layer for every encrypted sort key, bounded by the roughly 1500-row dataset where this is sub-millisecond. Amounts additionally lose range filtering at the database level, which moves to the same path. This constrains cursor pagination: cursors apply only to due_date, reference_id and created_at now that amount is encrypted. Document the boundary at each endpoint. Acceptance: A2.1 passes for both alphabetical and numerical sorting, and endpoints sorting by an encrypted column return correctly ordered pages.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Scaffold React SPA with Chakra UI
Description: Set up the React 18 SPA with React Router, ChakraProvider, TanStack Query for server state, and Zustand for UI state. Configure the Vercel build. Acceptance: the app builds, deploys to a preview URL, and renders an authenticated shell.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Implement Supabase Auth flow in React
Description: Build signup, login, logout, session refresh, and protected routes using Supabase Auth. Handle token refresh transparently and redirect on 401. Acceptance: a user can sign up, log in, refresh across a token expiry, and log out cleanly.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Build login route with AuthForm
Description: Create the /login route, the only screen without the app shell. AuthForm has idle, submitting and error variants with field-level validation. Submit disables while in flight so a double-submit cannot create two sessions. A failed attempt preserves typed input. Acceptance: login succeeds, wrong credentials give a generic non-enumerating failure, and the e2e persona B signup and login checks pass.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Build AuthProvider and RoleGate
Description: AuthProvider owns session, MeResponse and status, and handles transparent token refresh. RoleGate takes allow (Role array), an optional fallback and children, with hide, disable and redirect variants. Both are agent-blind and must not import from finhive/agent. Acceptance: a viewer navigating to an owner-only control sees the fallback, and the server still returns 403 if the control is bypassed.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Port MVP1 status colour palette to Chakra semantic tokens
Description: Define semantic tokens for status.active, status.overdue, status.pending, and status.paidoff with light and dark variants, carrying the MVP1 palette forward. Enforce the MVP1 rule that no component contains a hardcoded hex value. Acceptance: an eslint rule blocks raw hex colours in component files.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Dashboard placeholder page
Description: Milestone one does not require a populated dashboard. Ship the route, the app shell integration and the nav entry with a clearly-marked placeholder so navigation is complete and the shell is exercised. The real KPI strip reading the dbt mart lands in M5. Acceptance: /dashboard renders inside the shell, is reachable from the nav, and states plainly that metrics arrive in a later milestone.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Chat placeholder page
Description: Milestone one needs the chat route to exist without an agent behind it. Ship the route, the shell integration and a placeholder that says what the assistant will do once M2 lands. No LiteLLM, no Groq, no tool registry, and no spend. Acceptance: /chat renders in the shell and makes no outbound model call.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Build MDX content pipeline and help route
Description: Set up the MDX build so content lives in git, is reviewed in PRs and is versioned with the code. Vite emits a build-time content index and changelog manifest. Create /help with DocNav from the manifest, MDXRenderer with lazy code-split imports, on-this-page anchors and ChangelogList. This route has zero authorization, so pair it with the crawlability decisions in the Bot Readiness sweep. Acceptance: help content renders, the nav is generated from the manifest, and a missing slug shows a not-found state.

Milestone: FinHive M1a · Local Setup, Login & Encryption
Title: Prove encryption at rest before any real data lands
Description: The gate that makes the M1a encryption claim checkable rather than asserted. Inspect the database file and the wire directly: no plaintext borrower or depositor name appears in any table, index, or WAL segment; a row read back through the app returns the correct plaintext; a tampered ciphertext is rejected by the GCM auth tag; and the blind index returns the right rows for an exact filter. Run this BEFORE the M1b data import so no real record is ever written unencrypted. Acceptance: all four assertions pass and the test is wired into CI.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Import MVP1 git-tracked data into the local database
Description: The MVP1 user's live data is shared via git as CSV. Provide a one-command import that reads the git-tracked data, assigns the service account's org_id, and loads it into the local database, reusing the SQLite-to-Supabase migration's verification: row counts and per-record checksums reconciled before commit, abort on mismatch, source untouched. The import is idempotent so it can be re-run after a git pull. Acceptance: the user's real records appear on the Loans page and reconcile exactly with the CSV.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Implement PostgresLoanRepository with raw SQL
Description: Implement the MVP1 ILoanRepository interface using raw parameterized asyncpg queries. All SQL lives in module-level constants using numbered bind parameters. No f-strings, string concatenation, or .format() in any SQL. Acceptance: all MVP1 repository contract tests pass against Postgres.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Port loan use cases to async
Description: Convert the MVP1 use cases (CreateLoan, UpdateLoan, DeleteLoan, ExtendLoan, MarkPaidOff, RecomputeAllStatuses, GetLoans, GetAutocomplete) to async while preserving their contracts and tests. Acceptance: use case behaviour is identical to MVP1 and all ported tests pass.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Build loan CRUD REST endpoints
Description: Expose the loan use cases as REST endpoints with Pydantic request and response models and auto-generated OpenAPI. The OpenAPI schema later feeds the agent tool registry, so descriptions must be accurate and user-facing. Acceptance: full CRUD works end to end against Supabase with RLS enforced.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Compute LoanTotals in the app layer over decrypted rows
Description: ADR-2.4. Amounts are encrypted, so SQL SUM is no longer available. Every loans list response still carries totals (count, principal, interest, outstanding) computed over exactly the filtered set — but the app decrypts the fetched rows and sums with Decimal rather than the database aggregating. The guarantee is preserved: the footer restates totals from the same payload, so the table and the total cannot disagree, which is the direct answer to MVP1's worst defect class. Constraint created: totals cannot be computed over a set larger than the one fetched, which is fine at 1500 rows and is the trigger to revisit at scale. Acceptance: TotalsFooter renders from response.totals, a filter change updates both in one round trip, and Decimal summation is exact.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Implement cursor pagination across all list endpoints
Description: Apply cursor pagination uniformly to the six list endpoints: loans, approvals, reports, report records, agent sessions and any future list. Offset is easier against raw SQL but produces duplicate and skipped rows under concurrent writes, and the approval queue mutates while it is read. Mixed pagination is the worst outcome, so pick one and apply it everywhere. Acceptance: every list response carries next_cursor and a concurrent-write test shows no duplicate or skipped rows.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Implement optimistic concurrency on inline edit
Description: PATCH /api/loans/{reference_id} takes an If-Match version header and returns 409 on staleness. Add the version column, the conflict detection, and the LoanRow conflict variant that lets the user see both values and choose. Last-write-wins is cheaper but silently loses a bookkeeper's edit, which is the failure mode MVP1 existed to remove. Acceptance: two concurrent edits produce a 409 and a resolvable conflict state, not a silent overwrite.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Port report generation and approval endpoints
Description: Port the MVP1 report lifecycle (calculate, generate, approve, decline) to FastAPI, preserving the duplicate-reference and deleted-loan conflict warnings. Acceptance: the MVP1 approval flow integration tests pass against the new API.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Implement server-computed FieldDiff
Description: The approvals detail endpoint returns diff as a FieldDiff array alongside the raw before_state and after_state snapshots. The client must never derive the diff itself. Two diff implementations will disagree eventually, and what the user approves must be exactly what the server applies. Acceptance: DiffTable renders only from the server-provided FieldDiff, and a test proves the client has no diffing logic.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Implement bulk extend as a proposal batch
Description: POST /api/loans/extend takes reference_ids, periods and an optional reason and returns 202 with a batch_id. A bulk extend is a proposal even when a human initiated it from the table: form-originated and agent-originated writes converge on the same approval gate and differ only by OriginBadge. There must be no second unaudited write path. Acceptance: bulk extend from the table creates a pending batch and changes no loan row until approved.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Implement report generation async job path
Description: POST /api/reports returns 202 with job_id and poll_after_ms above the async threshold, or 200 with the report inline below it. Freeze REPORT_ASYNC_THRESHOLD at 100 records as a named constant referenced by the Playwright fixture boundary so both the sync and async paths are exercised. This is the only screen where the serverless timeout ceiling becomes user-visible. Acceptance: a 500-record report completes via the job path without a timeout and a 20-record report returns inline.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Implement long-running job escape hatch
Description: For report generation over 100 records, write a job row and return 202 Accepted with a client poll endpoint, avoiding the serverless timeout ceiling. Acceptance: a 500-record report completes via the job path without a timeout.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Implement report record preview and PDF export
Description: GET /api/reports/{report_id}/records returns paginated records plus totals for a read-only preview showing post-approval state. POST /api/reports/{report_id}/export returns a Vercel Blob signed URL with an expiry and byte count. Acceptance: the preview reconciles with the generated report and the PDF downloads via the signed URL.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Implement submit report to approval queue
Description: POST /api/reports/{report_id}/submit returns 202 with a batch_id, reusing the section 12 approval gate rather than introducing a parallel path. Acceptance: submitting a report produces a pending proposal batch visible on /approvals with a FORM origin badge.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Move amount non-negativity enforcement into Money
Description: ADR-2.4. CHECK (amount >= 0) cannot run on ciphertext and the column becomes BYTEA, so the database type guarantee is gone too. The Money value object lifted from MVP1 becomes the ONLY enforcement of non-negativity and integrality, which raises it from a nicety to the sole guard. Add a test asserting Money rejects every invalid construction — negative, fractional, non-numeric, overflow — and assert that the repository layer never constructs an amount without going through it. Acceptance: no code path can write a negative or fractional amount, proven by test rather than by convention.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Multi-month ByMonth filter in the MVP2 calculator
Description: Carry the MVP1 multi-select ByMonth behaviour into the MVP2 calculator and report generator. The filter parameter becomes a list of months rather than a single value, the API accepts repeated or comma-separated month params, and the UI uses multi-selection checkboxes. Success metric is identical to the MVP1 ticket: with several months selected, every loan whose due_date month falls in ANY selected month appears and no others. ByMonth still excludes no-due-date records, still scopes to the current calendar year, and still includes Overdue. Acceptance: parity with the MVP1 implementation on the same dataset, verified by the e2e MVP1 continuity sweep check A5.8.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Build loans table with filter and sort
Description: Recreate the MVP1 View Tab as a React data table: sortable columns, per-column filtering including the year to month date hierarchy, inline editing, and status colour coding. Carry forward the MVP1 lesson that filter state needs a single source of truth. Acceptance: filter behaviour matches the MVP1 sample data checkpoints (bg3 returns 2 records, dg3 returns 4).

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Build loan entry and edit forms
Description: Port the MVP1 Entry Tab: autocomplete on borrower and depositor fields, group auto-fill from history, due_period to due_date derivation, and date pickers. Acceptance: all MVP1 entry validation rules hold, including lowercase normalisation at write time.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Build reports route with generate form
Description: Create /reports with ReportForm (mode, period type, rates, selection) validating before submit, and ReportList showing generated and pending reports. Variants: interest, commission, tds, chq. Acceptance: a report generates end to end and appears in the list.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Build JobProgress polling component
Description: JobProgress takes a job_id and polls GET /api/reports/jobs/{job_id} with backoff, showing queued, running, done and failed states. Acceptance: progress advances visibly, a failure surfaces its error, and the poll stops on a terminal state.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Build mutation approval queue UI
Description: Create the approvals route rendering exact field-by-field before and after diffs from the stored JSONB snapshots, never the agent's prose description. Only the owner role sees approve controls, enforced server-side by RLS. Acceptance: a bookkeeper cannot approve, an owner can, and approving applies all mutations in a batch inside one transaction.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Build SessionExpiredDialog with edit replay
Description: On a 401 with code token_expired after a failed refresh, show a modal over the frozen screen. Unsaved inline edits are held in a buffer and replayed after re-auth. No route change and no data loss. MVP1 existed partly to stop silent data loss, so an expiry that discards a half-typed row reintroduces the original problem. Acceptance: an inline edit interrupted by an expiry survives re-auth and commits.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Add query result shape contract tests
Description: For every raw SQL query, add a test asserting the returned column set and types match the corresponding Pydantic model. This replaces the type safety an ORM would have provided. Acceptance: changing a column type in a migration without updating the model fails CI.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Add N+1 query detection tests
Description: Every list endpoint gets a test asserting an exact query count. Prevents the classic N+1 regression that raw SQL makes easy to introduce. Acceptance: adding a per-row lookup inside a loop fails the count assertion.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Set up Playwright e2e suite
Description: Configure Playwright to run against the Vercel preview deployment rather than a local server, so tests exercise the real edge and CDN behaviour. Acceptance: the suite runs in CI against the PR preview URL and blocks merge on failure.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: Write core e2e user journeys
Description: Cover the critical paths: sign up and log in, create a loan via the form, filter and sort the loans table, ask the agent a read-only question, request a mutation and approve it as owner, and confirm a bookkeeper cannot approve. Acceptance: all journeys pass against the preview deployment.

Milestone: FinHive M1b · MVP1 Parity — Read then Write
Title: MVP1 parity e2e sweep against the web app
Description: Run the e2e-testing skill's Persona A continuity sweep against the milestone-one web app: roughly 80 checks over entry, view, status engine, reference IDs, calculator, approvals, import/export, infrastructure behaviour and the deliberate UI/UX decisions. Any red in the calculation checks (A5) or the infrastructure checks (A8) blocks the milestone. This is the gate that proves the rewrite lost nothing, and it is the reason the MVP1 user can trust the web app enough to validate business on it. Acceptance: the sweep report shows PARITY HELD with no unexplained degradations.

Title: Add Vercel cron warming for hot bundles
Description: Add a Vercel Cron job pinging the agent and loans function bundles every five minutes during business hours to mitigate the 3 to 5 second Python cold start. At 3 DAU most requests would otherwise be cold. Acceptance: p95 latency during business hours drops measurably on the API Health dashboard.

Title: Add eslint rule forbidding gated components in agent-rendered subtrees
Description: Write a local eslint rule that fails CI when a component declared gated appears in the JSX of a component declared rendered. If DecisionBar could render inside TraceStep, the agent would control the pixels of its own approval control — the UI-layer equivalent of letting it write to the database. This is the rule that stops an innocent approve-from-chat ticket from shipping. Acceptance: a PR placing DecisionBar inside TraceStep is blocked with a named reason.

Title: Build PII masking pipeline
Description: Implement session-scoped bidirectional PII substitution: borrower_name, depositor_name, and account_number are replaced with stable tokens before any LLM call and rehydrated in the response. Tokens must be stable within a session so the agent can reason across turns. Amounts, dates, reference IDs, and statuses are never masked. Acceptance: no plaintext personal name appears in any outbound LLM payload, verified by a test that inspects the serialised request.

Title: Add a maskable-field classification test
Description: Under ARB decision OQ-01, PII masking is the control that keeps personal data inside India, so a new field carrying a name or identifier that is added without masking is a cross-border disclosure. Add a test that enumerates every string field on every model and fails unless each is explicitly classified as maskable or non-maskable. This makes the omission impossible rather than unlikely. Acceptance: adding an unclassified string field to a model fails CI with a message naming the field.

Title: Tokenise amounts before LLM egress
Description: ADR-2.4 decision 12 (APPROVED). Extend the session-scoped tokeniser from names to financial values: an amount becomes AMOUNT_1, rehydrated on the way out, exactly as PERSON_1 already works. Tokens are stable within a session so the agent can refer back across turns. This keeps the at-rest and in-transit postures consistent — encrypting a value in the database and then posting it to a US inference provider is a posture that would otherwise need explaining. Acceptance: no raw financial figure appears in any outbound LLM payload, verified by inspecting the serialised request, and the rendered answer shows real amounts.

Title: Implement agent suggestions endpoint
Description: GET /api/agent/suggestions returns surface-scoped prompt chips (id, label, prompt) powering AgentTeaser on the dashboard and the empty state on /chat. The agent must say what it can do before the user has to guess. Acceptance: dashboard and chat render suggestions and clicking one sends that prompt.

Title: Build agent chat UI
Description: Create the chat route rendering the streamed ReAct trace: thoughts, tool calls with arguments, observations, and the final answer. Showing the reasoning is the trust mechanism, not a loading state. Include a per-turn thumbs up and down control. Acceptance: a user can watch each reasoning step appear and submit feedback on any turn.

Title: Build component registry with agent-class declarations
Description: Create components/registry.ts declaring an agent class for every component: rendered, authored, drivable, gated or blind (ARD v2.1.0 section 4). Each class carries a rule — rendered treats all content as untrusted and never uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML; authored renders only from server-provided structured data; drivable must behave identically whether a change came from a form or a turn; gated must be authorized server-side independent of its own render; blind must not import from finhive/agent. Acceptance: every component in the 31-item inventory has a declared class.

Title: Build step-cap degraded answer treatment
Description: When MAX_STEPS is exhausted, return a partial answer plus two concrete rewrites of the question. Never a timeout error. The final event carries truncated true and reason step_cap so the client can distinguish this from a normal completion without string-matching. Acceptance: a deliberately unanswerable question degrades gracefully with actionable suggestions.

Title: Build cost budget soft-block treatment
Description: On a 429 with code budget_soft_block, the composer goes read-only stating the remaining budget and resets_at, and offers a form-based path to the same task. The owner is notified rather than the user silently blocked. A cost cap that only says no makes the product feel broken; routing to the same outcome without the model is the difference between a limit and a wall. Acceptance: exceeding the daily cap shows the state and the form path completes the task.

Title: Build RetryNotice in the ReAct trace
Description: When a tool call fails Pydantic validation, surface a collapsed line inside the trace such as corrected due_date — was next quarter. Shown, not hidden. Two attempts then degrade. Variants: attempt 1, attempt 2, degraded. Acceptance: a deliberately malformed tool argument produces a visible retry line and the loop recovers.

Title: Set up LiteLLM gateway with Groq
Description: Configure LiteLLM as the LLM abstraction layer pointing at Groq. Centralise model selection, retry policy, and timeout configuration so the provider stays swappable. Acceptance: a completion round-trips through LiteLLM and usage data is returned in normalised form.

Title: Build typed tool registry
Description: Implement the @tool decorator and registry: each tool declares a Pydantic args model, a mutating flag, and a required_role. Generate the JSON schema handed to Groq from the Pydantic models so schema and implementation cannot drift. Acceptance: registering a tool automatically exposes a correct JSON schema and role gate.

Title: Implement read-only agent tools
Description: Build get_current_context, resolve_entity, query_loans, get_portfolio_summary, and calculate_interest. All are non-mutating and execute immediately. resolve_entity is RAG-backed for fuzzy name resolution. Acceptance: each tool returns correctly shaped output and respects RLS for the calling user.

Title: Implement the ReAct loop
Description: Build the core reason-act-observe loop with MAX_STEPS of 6, Pydantic validation of every tool call before dispatch, and a maximum of 2 retries per step on validation failure with the error fed back as an observation. On step exhaustion return partial results with a refinement prompt, never a timeout error. Acceptance: the loop resolves the canonical quarterly query in 4 steps and degrades gracefully when capped.

Title: Implement SSE streaming for agent responses
Description: Stream thought, action, observation, proposal, and final events over Server-Sent Events. Set X-Accel-Buffering no and Cache-Control no-transform to prevent CDN buffering. Acceptance: the first event reaches the browser within one second and each ReAct step renders as it completes.

Title: Implement viewer read-only agent access
Description: ARB decision OQ-03 grants the viewer role agent access restricted to the 7 read-only tools; mutating tools stay bookkeeper and above. The Composer stays present for viewers — the restriction is enforced by required_role on the @tool decorator, server-side, not by hiding the input. Because a viewer's tool set is a strict subset, the role becomes a natural test fixture: any turn producing a proposal under a viewer JWT is an unsafe-call failure with an unambiguous cause. Acceptance: a viewer can ask what is overdue and receive an answer, and no viewer turn can ever emit a proposal event.

Title: Implement search_help agent tool with MDX RAG
Description: Add a read-only tool doing retrieval over the /help MDX content so the agent answers questions about the product's own rules from versioned docs rather than from the model's memory of them. This closes the loop where hallucination is most likely. Required role viewer, non-mutating. Acceptance: asking how extend works returns an answer grounded in the MDX with a citation.

Title: Make chat empty results name the applied filter
Description: When an agent query returns zero rows, the answer must state which filter produced nothing rather than implying no such records exist. If the agent filtered on sharma_traders and found nothing, saying no loans found is a lie by omission — and it is the failure mode that destroys trust in an agent fastest. Acceptance: a zero-row agent answer names the filter and offers to broaden it.

Title: Create pgvector schema and business rule embeddings
Description: Migration 0005: add the schema_embeddings table with pgvector. Embed the loan schema, field semantics, and MVP1 business rules (giving_date is never used in calculations, the interest formulas, the status transition rules) for intent routing and grounding. Acceptance: resolve_entity and schema questions retrieve relevant context with usable similarity scores.

Title: Implement LLM budget guardrails
Description: Add spend caps: 8000 prompt tokens per turn (truncate RAG context and warn), 0.50 USD per user per day (soft block and notify), and 10 USD per org per month (hard block and page). Acceptance: exceeding each threshold triggers the specified behaviour and emits a metric.

Title: Implement list_reports agent tool
Description: Add a read-only tool exposing report status so the agent can answer questions like whether last month's report went through. Required role viewer, non-mutating. Acceptance: the tool returns report summaries respecting RLS for the calling user and appears in the registry as READ.

Title: Tools compute, the agent narrates — no LLM arithmetic
Description: ADR-2.4 decision 12. With amounts tokenised, the agent cannot and must not perform arithmetic on financial values. Move all computation server-side: get_portfolio_summary decrypts and sums with Decimal returning a token; query_loans sorts and ranks server-side returning rows already ordered; calculate_interest uses the MVP1 calculator. The agent narrates results it did not compute. This is a correctness improvement as much as a compliance one — LLMs are unreliable at arithmetic and this application is about money. Known cost: any question needing magnitude reasoning the tools did not pre-compute becomes unanswerable until a tool is added, and this will surface as eval failures that look like capability gaps rather than bugs. Acceptance: no tool returns a raw figure for the model to operate on, and an eval case asking which borrower owes the most is answered from server-side ranking.

Title: Build agent evaluation harness
Description: Create the golden dataset format and runner: YAML cases specifying input, expected tool sequence, expected arguments, must_not_call assertions, required answer content, and max steps. Report tool-selection accuracy, argument accuracy, task completion, unsafe-call rate, p95 latency, and cost per task. Acceptance: the harness runs locally and in CI and produces a scored report.

Title: Seed golden eval dataset with canonical queries
Description: Author the initial eval cases covering the three canonical user journeys: querying quarterly dues by group, creating a loan conversationally, and batch-extending overdue loans. Include negative cases asserting that read-only questions never invoke mutating tools. Acceptance: at least 20 cases covering all nine tools.

Title: Add SSE streaming e2e assertion
Description: Add a Playwright test asserting the first SSE event arrives within one second of sending a chat message. This is the guard against a future CDN or header configuration change silently breaking streaming and destroying the core UX. Acceptance: removing the X-Accel-Buffering header fails this test.

Title: Add Playwright assertion for the agent-class invariant
Description: With a pending proposal open in /chat, assert that elements carrying data-agent-class=gated have count zero inside the react-trace container. This is the runtime counterpart to the eslint rule and catches dynamic composition the static rule cannot see. Acceptance: the assertion fails if a gated control is rendered into the trace at runtime.

Title: Implement per-turn token and cost metering
Description: Capture prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost_usd via litellm.completion_cost, model, per-step and total latency_ms, and the full react_trace JSONB into agent_turns on every turn. This table is the substrate for observability, cost tracking, and the eval dataset. Acceptance: every agent turn produces a complete, queryable metrics row.

Title: Document the deliberate tool exclusions
Description: Add explicit NOT A TOOL comments in finhive/agent/registry.py for approve_batch, revert_batch and export_report, each with its reason. approve_batch: the agent must never operate its own gate. revert_batch: a hallucinated revert silently undoes a decision a human made deliberately, with no second human in the loop — strictly worse than a hallucinated proposal. export_report: writes a file to Blob and costs money per call, so a looping agent could fill the store. The absence of a tool is invisible; the reason for its absence should not be. Acceptance: the comments exist and are referenced from the ARD.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Pin Vercel functions to the bom1 region
Description: ARB decision OQ-01 puts primary data in ap-south-1 (Mumbai). Serverless functions default to iad1 (Washington), which would add roughly 200-250ms round trip to EVERY database query — a request making four queries pays a second of latency before doing any work, and at 3 DAU most requests are already cold. Set regions to bom1 in vercel.json. Do this in Phase 1, before anyone measures performance and wrongly concludes the raw-SQL layer is slow. Acceptance: deployed functions report bom1 and p95 query latency is single-digit ms to the database.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Add a region mismatch startup assertion
Description: Log the function region and the database region together at startup and fail loudly on a mismatch. A silent region drift is invisible until someone investigates a latency chart weeks later. Acceptance: a deliberately mismatched configuration is caught at boot with a clear message naming both regions.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Provision Supabase projects in ap-south-1
Description: Create finhive-prod and finhive-staging Supabase projects in the ap-south-1 (Mumbai) region per ARB decision OQ-01 — SMB users are in India and primary data resides there. Configure connection pooling and store credentials in GitHub Secrets and Vercel environment variables. Acceptance: both projects report region ap-south-1, are reachable from CI, and the anon and service_role keys are stored as secrets, never committed.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Build data migration script from SQLite to Supabase
Description: Write migrate_to_supabase.py: export from the MVP1 SQLite database, assign org_id, insert into Postgres, then verify row counts and per-record checksums before committing. Abort and leave SQLite untouched on any mismatch. Acceptance: migration is idempotent, verified, and a deliberately corrupted source aborts cleanly.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Configure Vercel Blob for report PDFs and imports
Description: Wire Vercel Blob for report PDF storage and CSV/XLSX upload. Use signed direct uploads from the browser to bypass the serverless request body size limit. Acceptance: a report PDF is generated, stored, and retrievable via a signed URL, and a 5MB XLSX uploads successfully.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Encrypt cold archive partitions in Blob
Description: ADR-2.4 plus ARB decision OQ-02. The 7-year cold archive holds proposed_mutations and agent_turns snapshots, which contain NPI. Compressed JSONL partitions written to Blob must be encrypted at rest with the same key hierarchy, and the restore procedure must decrypt and verify. An archive is the longest-lived copy of this data, so it cannot be the weakest protected. Acceptance: an archived partition is unreadable without the key and the quarterly restore test decrypts and reconciles row-level equality.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Implement Row Level Security policies
Description: Migration 0003: enable RLS on all tenant tables. Add tenant isolation policies keyed on the org_id JWT claim, and a role-gated policy allowing only owner to update reports to approved status. Acceptance: policies are active on every business table and a direct query without a JWT claim returns zero rows.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Restrict service_role key to a single guarded module
Description: The Supabase service_role key bypasses RLS entirely. Confine it to finhive/db/admin.py, guarded by an environment variable that is absent from every serverless bundle except api/admin. Add a ruff rule banning imports of the service-role client anywhere else. Acceptance: importing the admin client from any other module fails lint.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Implement transactional proposal application
Description: Build the approval handler: on approve, apply every after_state in the batch inside a single Postgres transaction so partial application is impossible. Retain before_state to make any batch reversible. Acceptance: a deliberately failing mid-batch mutation rolls back the entire batch.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Implement approval revert endpoint
Description: Add POST /api/approvals/{batch_id}/revert taking a reason and inverting from the retained before_state inside one transaction. ARD section 12 promised reversibility, but without a route that promise resolves to someone writing SQL against production, which is not a control. This is deliberately NOT an agent tool. Acceptance: an applied batch reverts cleanly, the receipt shows the reverting transaction id, and no agent tool can reach this route.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Implement OriginBadge provenance marking
Description: OriginBadge renders AGENT (amber) or FORM (blue) wherever a change is shown: chat proposal cards, the dashboard approval feed and the approvals batch header. Amber means one thing everywhere — a model originated this — and is never reused for anything else. Provenance is not status. Acceptance: every proposal surface carries the badge and a reviewer can tell origin at a glance.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Build RLS-denied treatment on approvals
Description: When a non-owner opens a pending batch, the diff stays fully visible and DecisionBar is replaced by an explanation plus a request-approval action. The button is absent, not disabled with a tooltip. The 403 carries code rls_denied and required_role so the client renders the right message without parsing prose. Acceptance: a bookkeeper sees the full diff, no approve control, and a working request-approval action.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Build the component inventory with all variants
Description: Implement the 31 components from ARD v2.1.0 section 6 with every declared variant. Variants are the contract: a component without its states designed is one that will be improvised under deadline. Includes Button, StatusChip, OriginBadge, FilterChip, KpiCard, DataTable, TableRow, Input/DateField, SegmentedControl, Drawer, Dialog, Toast, Pagination and the agent components. Acceptance: every variant renders in isolation and is visually reviewable.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Build skeleton states matching real row geometry
Description: Skeleton variants (text, row, card, trace) must match the geometry of the real content so nothing shifts when data lands. At 3 DAU most requests are cold, so the loading state is the common case, not an edge case. Never a centred spinner. Acceptance: a layout-shift assertion shows no CLS when data replaces a skeleton.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Build EmptyState variants that name the cause
Description: EmptyState has no-data, no-results, no-permission and error variants. The no-results variant restates the filter that produced nothing and offers to clear it. A zero-row answer must never read as none exist. Acceptance: filtering to zero rows shows the applied filter and a working clear action.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Implement mutating agent tools as proposals
Description: Build create_loan, update_loan, extend_loan, and generate_report. These must never execute directly. The dispatcher writes a proposed_mutations row with full before_state and after_state JSONB snapshots. Acceptance: invoking any mutating tool produces a proposal row and leaves the loans table untouched.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Write RLS cross-tenant isolation test
Description: Create the single most important security test in the repo: seed two orgs, authenticate as a user in Org A, and assert that every read and write path returns zero rows or a permission error for Org B's data. Must run against a real ephemeral Supabase branch, never a mock. Acceptance: the test fails if RLS is disabled on any table.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Gate CI on agent eval thresholds
Description: Enforce eval gates in CI: tool-selection accuracy at least 90 percent, argument accuracy at least 85 percent, task completion at least 85 percent, p95 latency at most 4 seconds, cost per task at most 0.001 USD, and unsafe-call rate exactly 0 percent as a hard release blocker. Run the full suite nightly and a fast subset per PR. Acceptance: a regression that causes one unrequested mutation proposal fails the build.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Test DiffRow type-mismatch variant
Description: before_state and after_state are JSONB, so the schema can drift between when a proposal is written and when it is approved. The design treats this as a rendered state rather than a crash. Write the test that forces a type mismatch between snapshots and assert the row renders its type-mismatch variant with both values legible. Acceptance: a proposal whose target schema changed after creation renders safely and does not block the rest of the batch.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Add agent-class test plan coverage
Description: The agent-class taxonomy generates the test plan. Agent-rendered components need prompt and markup injection tests. Agent-authored need server-truth tests proving they never render agent prose. Agent-gated need server-side authorization tests. Agent-blind need an assertion that they do not import from finhive/agent. Acceptance: each of the five classes has at least one test enforcing its rule.

Milestone: FinHive M3 · Agent Write, UI Polish & Hosted Infra
Title: Build feedback-to-eval pipeline
Description: Wire the thumbs-down loop: capture the react_trace, provide a triage workflow classifying the failure as prompt, tool, or data, and add the case to the golden dataset as a permanent regression test. Acceptance: a thumbs-down turn can be converted into an eval case in one step and the nightly suite proves the fix holds.

Title: Production deployment to Vercel
Description: Deploy to production on Vercel with functions pinned to bom1 and the Supabase ap-south-1 project, environment separation for production, staging and per-PR previews, and secrets in Vercel environment variables rather than the repo. Acceptance: production is reachable over HTTPS, reports its region, and a PR preview deploys against an ephemeral database branch.

Title: Implement log scrubbing before Grafana export
Description: Grafana Cloud processes outside India. Under ARB decision OQ-01 a correlation ID in a log line is fine but a borrower name is a cross-border transfer of personal data. Add a scrubbing filter over the OTLP log exporter covering every field classified as maskable, and a test asserting no personal identifier reaches the exporter. Acceptance: a log line containing a borrower name is scrubbed before export and the test fails if the filter is bypassed.

Title: Public signup and multi-user authentication
Description: Replace the M1 service-account shortcut with the real signup flow: email and password signup, verification, password reset, and non-enumerating failures on duplicate email and wrong password. Acceptance: a new user signs up unaided and the e2e Persona B signup and session checks pass.

Title: Role assignment and invitation flow
Description: Let an owner invite a user into their org and assign bookkeeper or viewer. Role restrictions are already enforced server-side by RLS and the tool registry's required_role; this ticket adds the assignment surface, not the enforcement. Acceptance: an owner invites a bookkeeper, the invitee's JWT carries the role, and the approvals decision bar is absent for them at both the UI and the API.

Title: Second-user onboarding and collision validation
Description: Onboard one additional user and prove the system carries no data or workflow collisions: two orgs cannot see each other's loans; reference ID counters are per-org and do not interleave; two users editing the same loan produce a clean 409 rather than a silent overwrite; two pending proposals touching the same loan warn on approval; and the approval queue does not leak batches across orgs. This is the milestone-four exit gate. Acceptance: every collision scenario has a passing test and a written result.

Title: Bot Readiness sweep before external exposure
Description: Run the e2e-testing skill's Persona C sweep — 67 checks across secret and PII exposure, unauthenticated crawl, the click-everything pass, accessibility, crawlability, hostile input and cost abuse — against the staging deployment before any external user is given access. Any S1 in secrets, unauthenticated access or prompt injection means NOT READY, with no exceptions. Acceptance: the report verdict is READY and every S2 is either fixed or explicitly accepted with a reason.

Title: Instrument FastAPI with OpenTelemetry
Description: Add OTLP traces, metrics, and logs export to Grafana Cloud (Tempo, Prometheus, Loki). Propagate a correlation ID from the browser through the API to the agent loop. Acceptance: a single user request is traceable end to end including every ReAct step.

Title: Implement Amplitude event instrumentation
Description: Emit the event taxonomy from the metrics spec: loan_created, agent_turn_completed, agent_feedback, mutation_proposed, mutation_approved, mutation_rejected, report_generated, and spreadsheet_op_replaced. The last one is the North Star input and must be emitted from both form and agent paths. Acceptance: all events appear in Amplitude with correct properties and WSOR is computable.

Title: Build Grafana dashboards
Description: Create four dashboards: API Health (rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, errors by route, cold starts), Agent Health (turns per hour, steps per turn, tool failure and retry rates, p95 loop latency), Cost (spend by user and day, tokens by model, cost per completed task), and Data Quality (dbt pass rate, mart row counts, freshness). Acceptance: all four dashboards render live data.

Title: Configure Grafana critical alerts
Description: Set alerts for API 5xx above 5 percent over 5 minutes, any agent unsafe tool call, cost anomaly above 3x the 7-day mean, any dbt contract test failure, and any cross-org read attempt in logs. Acceptance: each alert fires correctly against a synthetic trigger.

Title: Enable Vercel Analytics
Description: Turn on Vercel Analytics for Core Web Vitals and page performance. Acceptance: LCP, INP, and CLS are reported for all routes.

Title: Define North Star metric instrumentation spec
Description: Document the exact Amplitude event schema for Weekly Spreadsheet Operations Replaced (WSOR) before any code is written. Specify the spreadsheet_op_replaced event with op_type and method properties, plus the L2 supporting metrics (Agent Task Completion Rate, Time to Insight p95, Proposal Approval Rate, Data Trust Score, Cost per Resolved Task) and the three counter-metrics. Acceptance: a metrics spec doc is merged and every downstream ticket references the events it must emit.

Title: Wire dbt into GitHub Actions
Description: Run dbt build on every PR touching models/ and nightly against production. Post results to the PR and export test outcomes to Grafana. dbt never runs inside a Vercel function. Acceptance: a failing contract test blocks the PR and appears on the data quality dashboard.

Title: Build dbt project with staging models
Description: Initialise the dbt project against Supabase Postgres. Build stg_loans and stg_payments with typing and normalisation. Acceptance: dbt build succeeds locally and in CI.

Title: Build dbt marts with enforced contracts
Description: Build dim_borrower, fct_loan_schedule (monthly, quarterly, yearly), fct_outstanding_balance, and agg_portfolio_summary with contract enforcement enabled so a type change fails the build. Acceptance: altering a column type in a mart without updating the contract fails dbt build.

Title: Add dbt test asserting MVP1 interest formula
Description: Add an expression_is_true test asserting interest_accrued equals principal times rate times periods divided by 1200 for monthly rows. This gives the core business rule a second independent enforcer at the data layer, so Python and warehouse logic cannot silently diverge. Acceptance: changing the Python calculator without updating dbt fails CI, and vice versa.

Title: Add is_due_soon to the portfolio mart
Description: Extend the dbt mart with the is_due_soon derived field and its configurable day window, contract-enforced like every other mart column. The dashboard and the loans table both read it so a due-soon count cannot disagree between screens. Acceptance: dbt contract enforcement covers the new column and both surfaces reconcile.

Title: Implement retention tiering for audit tables
Description: ARB decision OQ-02 sets 7-year retention for proposed_mutations, agent_turns, reports and report_records. Postgres is the wrong home for year six: proposed_mutations holds full before_state and after_state JSONB per record per batch and is the fastest-growing table in the system. Implement tiering — hot in Postgres for 0-12 months, cold as compressed JSONL in Blob partitioned by month for 12 months to 7 years. Keeps the approvals queue fast in year five. Acceptance: a scheduled job moves aged rows to cold storage and the hot table stays bounded.

Title: Build the archive index table
Description: Retention without retrieval is not retention, and restoring an archive to answer a simple question is too slow to be used. Keep a pointer table in Postgres for the full 7 years carrying batch_id, reference_id, operation, decided_by, decided_at and archive_path. Then who extended this loan in 2027 is answerable without restoring anything; only the full before and after payload needs a restore. Acceptance: an archived batch is discoverable and attributable from the index alone.

Title: Write and test the archive restore procedure
Description: An archive nobody has restored from is a folder of files you believe contain something. Document the restore path and add a CI job that runs quarterly against a synthetic archive, restoring a month partition and asserting row-level equality with the original. Acceptance: the quarterly job passes and a deliberately corrupted archive fails it.

Title: Implement the 7-year purge job
Description: Without an actual deletion job, 7-year retention becomes indefinite retention by neglect — a different and in privacy terms worse policy than the one approved. Implement the purge for records past 7 years, with a dry-run mode, an audit line per purged partition, and a guard preventing a purge of anything inside the window. Acceptance: dry run reports the correct partitions and the guard blocks an in-window deletion attempt.

Title: Confirm Supabase backups are not the retention mechanism
Description: Supabase PITR is 7 days and is a recovery tool, not retention. Conflating the two is how an organisation discovers in year four that it has 7 days of history. Verify and document that the archive pipeline, not backups, satisfies ARB decision OQ-02, and that backup restore never overwrites archived partitions. Acceptance: the distinction is documented and a restore drill confirms archives survive a PITR restore.

Title: Move financial aggregation out of dbt into an app-layer job
Description: ADR-2.4. dbt is SQL in the warehouse, has no key, and cannot decrypt — so fct_outstanding_balance, agg_portfolio_summary and every amount-bearing mart cannot be computed there. Build an app-layer materialization job that decrypts, computes with Decimal, re-encrypts and writes the mart, scheduled in GitHub Actions alongside dbt rather than inside a Vercel function. dbt keeps what it can still enforce: column presence, types, nullability, enum validity, referential integrity, reference_id uniqueness, date logic, freshness, row counts and null rates. Acceptance: financial marts are produced and encrypted, and dbt's remaining contracts still fail the build on a shape violation.

Title: Implement DueSoon as a derived display state
Description: StatusChip has five variants but StatusEngine returns four and must keep returning four — it is fully tested, correct, and the thing this rewrite is obliged not to break. Compute DueSoon in the dbt mart as Active plus a due_date within N days, returned as a separate is_due_soon boolean, and render the chip from status equals Active and is_due_soon. Nothing writes DueSoon to loans.status; enforce with a CHECK constraint. N is configurable, not hardcoded. Acceptance: the four-value status engine and its tests are untouched, the constraint rejects a DueSoon write, and the chip renders correctly.

Title: Build portfolio dashboard
Description: Create the landing dashboard: total outstanding, count by status, upcoming dues, and overdue alerts. Read from the dbt aggregate mart rather than computing client-side. Acceptance: dashboard figures reconcile exactly with the loans table.

Title: Implement dbt status endpoint and DataHealthBadge
Description: GET /api/admin/dbt/status returns passed, total, last_run_at and the failing models. DataHealthBadge renders pass, degraded and stale variants in the nav rail footer. This surfaces the data contract state where a user will actually see it. Acceptance: a deliberately failing dbt test turns the badge degraded and names the failing model.

Title: Document erasure request handling under statutory retention
Description: DPDP grants data principals a right to erasure, but statutory retention overrides it for the retention period — and only for the records the statute covers. An erasure request must NOT be honoured by deleting rows from proposed_mutations or report_records inside the 7-year window, and must not be silently ignored either. Document the correct handling: refusal with a stated reason for in-scope records, plus deletion of anything outside statutory scope such as agent chat transcripts. Write it now while it is a design note rather than an incident. Acceptance: the procedure is documented and referenced from ARB_DECISIONS.md.

Title: Author MDX help content and onboarding
Description: Write the in-app help content in MDX covering first-run onboarding, what the agent can and cannot do, how the approval queue works, and the interest calculation rules. Content lives in git and is reviewed in PRs. Acceptance: the help route renders MDX and is linked from the app shell.

Title: Correct story bank S13 framing on desktop GUI
Description: The S13 story states the existing desktop GUI is Tkinter. The actual MVP1 implementation is PySide6 with QAbstractTableModel. Correct the story before it is used in an interview. Acceptance: S13 accurately describes the MVP1 stack.

Title: Property-based test replacing the dbt interest-formula assertion
Description: ADR-2.4 is honest that amount encryption weakens the v2.0.0 double-enforcement argument: the SQL assertion of the monthly interest formula dies, and two Python implementations can share a Python bug in a way a Python and a SQL implementation cannot. Narrow the gap with a property-based test — generate thousands of random amount, rate and period combinations and assert the app-layer materialization job and InterestCalculator agree exactly, including rounding at two decimal places with ROUND_HALF_UP. This catches divergence without restoring language independence, and the difference should be stated rather than glossed. Acceptance: the property test runs in CI and a deliberate off-by-one in either implementation fails it.
